epic_description: Ongoing maintenance of the ai-agent-workforce specialist agent roster: adding, retiring, or updating specialist agent definitions (Claude Code + opencode) as capability gaps are identified in the fleet of agents deployed by this repo's Ansible roles.
objective: Keep the deployed specialist-agent roster aligned with the actual engineering domains the team works in, so every project type has a purpose-built agent instead of a mismatched stand-in.

stories.name: Add native-macos-engineer specialist agent
stories.description:
As a platform maintainer of ai-agent-workforce, I want a dedicated native-macos-engineer specialist agent definition, so that native macOS app work (Swift 6, SwiftUI for macOS, AppKit, App Sandbox, security-scoped bookmarks, macOS-specific APIs such as NSStatusItem/NSPopover) is handled by an agent purpose-built for it, instead of being bolted onto mobile-engineer (which is scoped to iOS/Android/Flutter/React Native and does not cover App Sandbox entitlements, security-scoped bookmarks, or AppKit/macOS menu-bar-utility patterns).

---
Technical notes — exact scope, implement every item, nothing beyond this list without a change request:

1. Author roles/claude/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md (Claude Code agent definition). Match the structural conventions of the existing roles/claude/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md: YAML frontmatter with name, description, tools, model: sonnet (same value mobile-engineer.md uses), permissionMode: acceptEdits, maxTurns: 20, memory: project, and a skills: list. The skills: list must include a new skill named native-macos-engineering (see item 3) alongside the same supporting skills mobile-engineer.md lists (test-driven-development, git-commit, git-branch, dependency-review, run-quality-checks, shortcut, spike, threat-model, incident). Body sections, matching mobile-engineer.md's section structure: role summary, Language and Tone (Australian English spelling, no AI fluff — copy verbatim from mobile-engineer.md), Knowledge Base (see item 3), Non-Negotiable Standards, Development Workflow, What You Do NOT Tolerate, Collaboration (see item 4).

2. Author roles/opencode/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md (opencode agent definition). Match the structural conventions of the existing roles/opencode/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md: YAML frontmatter with description, mode: all, steps: 20, permission: block (edit: allow, bash: allow, skill: allow). Do NOT add a model: frontmatter field — none of the 12 existing opencode agent .md files declare one (confirmed by direct inspection of every file); the Kimi/GLM model tier described for opencode agents is documentation text only (in roles/opencode/files/opencode.jsonc comments and the create.yml debug message, see item 5), not a per-file enforced field anywhere in this repo, and this story must not invent a new enforcement mechanism that no other agent has. Body sections, matching mobile-engineer.md's structure: STEP 0 knowledge-base instruction (see item 3), Mandatory Rules, Workflow, Checklist, "When to hand off" (see item 4).

3. Author roles/skills/files/native-macos-engineering/SKILL.md, a new Knowledge Base skill covering: Swift 6 language features, SwiftUI for macOS (window/scene management, menu bar commands), AppKit (NSWindow, NSViewController, NSStatusItem, NSPopover, and other menu-bar/status-bar-utility patterns), App Sandbox entitlements, security-scoped bookmarks (persisting sandboxed file access across launches), and Mac App Store notarisation/distribution. Both new agent definitions' Knowledge Base section (Claude) / STEP 0 section (opencode) must reference this skill by its path, following the same pattern mobile-engineer.md uses for its own Knowledge Base line: "Load the [/native-macos-engineering](../skills/native-macos-engineering/SKILL.md) skill before writing, reviewing, or designing any native macOS code — it holds the full stack reference (...)". No edit to roles/skills/tasks/create.yml is required: that task deploys everything under roles/skills/files/ via a directory copy (src: "{{ role_path }}/files/") with no per-skill loop list to maintain — dropping the new native-macos-engineering/ directory under roles/skills/files/ is sufficient for it to be deployed automatically on the next playbook run.

4. Edit FOUR agent-definition files to add reciprocal hand-off boundaries — this story is not just "create two new files", it also requires editing the two existing mobile-engineer.md files:
   a. roles/claude/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md — in its existing "## Collaboration" section, add a new bullet: "macOS desktop apps (AppKit, App Sandbox, security-scoped bookmarks, menu-bar utilities, Mac App Store notarisation) → hand off to native-macos-engineer, even where the code is SwiftUI."
   b. roles/opencode/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md — in its existing "## When to hand off" section, add the same bullet, phrased to match that section's existing bullet style: "macOS desktop apps (AppKit, App Sandbox, security-scoped bookmarks, menu-bar utilities, Mac App Store notarisation) → hand off to native-macos-engineer, even where the code is SwiftUI."
   c. roles/claude/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md — in its "## Collaboration" section, add the reciprocal bullet: "iOS/iPadOS/watchOS/tvOS work, or shared SwiftUI code targeting those platforms → hand off to mobile-engineer, even where the code looks identical to macOS SwiftUI."
   d. roles/opencode/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md — in its "## When to hand off" section, add the same reciprocal bullet.

5. Model-routing tier: native-macos-engineer runs on the same model tier as mobile-engineer and frontend-developer — kimi-k2.7-code on the opencode side. (The Kimi/GLM split tracks domain shape — Apple-ecosystem client-app work vs. backend/systems work — not security sensitivity; mobile-engineer already owns security-adjacent work such as Keychain/biometrics on this tier.) On the Claude Code side, roles/claude/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md gets model: sonnet, the same frontmatter value roles/claude/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md already has (see item 1).
   - Update roles/claude/tasks/create.yml: add native-macos-engineer.md to the loop: list in the "Deploy Claude Code agents" task (currently 12 entries, alphabetically ordered — insert after mobile-engineer.md and before principal-engineer.md to preserve alphabetical order), and add a one-line entry to the ansible.builtin.debug "Display deployed agents" message block, in the same "- agent-name: one-line description" format as the other 12 lines, positioned alphabetically between the mobile-engineer and principal-engineer lines.
   - Update roles/opencode/tasks/create.yml: add native-macos-engineer.md to the loop: list in the "Deploy opencode agent markdown files" task (same alphabetical insertion point: after mobile-engineer.md, before principal-engineer.md), and add a one-line entry to the ansible.builtin.debug "Display deployed configuration" message block under the existing "Kimi implementation agents (kimi-k2.7-code):" heading, alongside the existing frontend-developer and mobile-engineer lines, in the same "- agent-name  full  one-line description" format.

6. Update roles/claude/files/CLAUDE.md's "## Agents" section (the routing table under "Use the specialist agents defined in `~/.claude/agents/`:" that currently lists 12 agents, one bullet per agent with a one-line description, in alphabetical order: architecture-guardian, backend-developer, business-analyst, data-engineer, frontend-developer, identity-security-developer, infrastructure-engineer, mobile-engineer, principal-engineer, qe-engineer, secops-engineer, sre-engineer) — add a 13th bullet for native-macos-engineer, in the same "- **agent-name** — one-line description" format as the existing 12, positioned alphabetically between mobile-engineer and principal-engineer. No corresponding edit is needed in roles/opencode/files/AGENTS.md: that file has no equivalent enumerated agent-routing list (confirmed by direct inspection — it contains only workflow/operating-rule sections, no "## Agents" section or per-agent bullet list). Do not add one there; that would be scope creep beyond this story.

Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this story (do not implement — this would be over-building beyond the agreed requirement):
- No edit to roles/claude/tasks/destroy.yml or roles/opencode/tasks/destroy.yml. Both remove their entire agents directory wholesale (state: absent on the directory itself, not a per-file loop), so adding the new file to the create-side loop (item 5) is sufficient — the destroy task removes it along with everything else in that directory with no further change needed.
- No bespoke file-permission handling. Both create.yml copy tasks already apply mode: '0600' to every file in their respective loop, with mode: '0700' already set on the parent agents directory. Once native-macos-engineer.md is added to the existing loop list (item 5), it inherits correct permissions automatically — do not write a separate copy task for this one file.

Separate note (not a blocking condition on this story, informational only): none of the 12 existing opencode agent .md files declare a model: frontmatter field — the Kimi/GLM tiering that create.yml's debug message describes is documentation text only, not an enforced mechanism anywhere in this repo today. This story is consistent with that existing (aspirational) documentation pattern and must not invent enforcement that doesn't exist elsewhere in the roster.
stories.acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Claude Code agent deployment path
Given the ai-agent-workforce Ansible playbook has been run against a target machine
When the "Deploy Claude Code agents" task in roles/claude/tasks/create.yml executes
Then a file named native-macos-engineer.md is present at ~/.claude/agents/native-macos-engineer.md with file mode 0600
And it is listed in the "Display deployed agents" debug message alongside the other 12 agents

Scenario: opencode agent deployment path (corrected location)
Given the ai-agent-workforce Ansible playbook has been run against a target machine
When the "Deploy opencode agent markdown files" task in roles/opencode/tasks/create.yml executes
Then a file named native-macos-engineer.md is present at ~/.config/opencode/agents/native-macos-engineer.md (plural "agents", matching every other opencode agent file — NOT the singular "~/.config/opencode/agent/" path that appeared in this story's original acceptance criteria, which was incorrect)
And it is listed under the "Kimi implementation agents (kimi-k2.7-code):" heading in the "Display deployed configuration" debug message, alongside frontend-developer and mobile-engineer

Scenario: Knowledge Base skill exists and is referenced correctly
Given roles/skills/files/native-macos-engineering/SKILL.md has been authored covering Swift 6, SwiftUI for macOS, AppKit, App Sandbox, security-scoped bookmarks, and NSStatusItem/NSPopover-class APIs
When the ai-agent-workforce Ansible playbook runs the "Deploy all local skills to central skills directory" task in roles/skills/tasks/create.yml
Then the skill is copied to ~/.skills/native-macos-engineering/SKILL.md with no change required to create.yml itself (it has no per-skill loop list)
And roles/claude/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md's Knowledge Base section references this skill by path in the same pattern as mobile-engineer.md's own Knowledge Base line
And roles/opencode/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md's STEP 0 section references this skill by path in the same pattern as mobile-engineer.md's own STEP 0 section

Scenario: mobile-engineer hands off macOS desktop work
Given a user asks mobile-engineer (Claude Code or opencode) to build a macOS menu-bar utility using AppKit and security-scoped bookmarks
When mobile-engineer reads its own hand-off guidance
Then roles/claude/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md's "## Collaboration" section contains a bullet directing macOS desktop app work (AppKit, App Sandbox, security-scoped bookmarks, menu-bar utilities, Mac App Store notarisation) to native-macos-engineer, even where the code is SwiftUI
And roles/opencode/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md's "## When to hand off" section contains the equivalent bullet

Scenario: native-macos-engineer hands off iOS/cross-Apple-platform work
Given a user asks native-macos-engineer to build a shared SwiftUI feature targeting iOS
When native-macos-engineer reads its own hand-off guidance
Then roles/claude/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md's "## Collaboration" section contains a bullet directing iOS/iPadOS/watchOS/tvOS work, or shared SwiftUI code targeting those platforms, to mobile-engineer, even where the code looks identical to macOS SwiftUI
And roles/opencode/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md's "## When to hand off" section contains the equivalent bullet

Scenario: model routing is consistent with the existing roster
Given roles/claude/files/agents/mobile-engineer.md declares model: sonnet in its frontmatter
When roles/claude/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md is authored
Then it also declares model: sonnet in its frontmatter
And roles/opencode/files/agents/native-macos-engineer.md does NOT declare any model: frontmatter field, consistent with all 12 existing opencode agent files
And roles/opencode/tasks/create.yml's debug message lists native-macos-engineer under the "Kimi implementation agents (kimi-k2.7-code):" heading, not under "Advisory agents" or "GLM implementation agents"

Scenario: global CLAUDE.md routing table updated
Given roles/claude/files/CLAUDE.md's "## Agents" section currently lists 12 specialist agents alphabetically
When this story is complete
Then it lists a 13th bullet for native-macos-engineer, positioned alphabetically between mobile-engineer and principal-engineer, in the same "- **agent-name** — one-line description" format as the existing entries
And roles/opencode/files/AGENTS.md is NOT modified, because it has no equivalent enumerated agent-routing section

Scenario: destroy and permissions require no additional changes
Given native-macos-engineer.md has been added to the loop: lists in both roles/claude/tasks/create.yml and roles/opencode/tasks/create.yml
When roles/claude/tasks/destroy.yml or roles/opencode/tasks/destroy.yml is run
Then the file is removed along with the rest of its parent agents directory with no destroy.yml edit required
And when create.yml is re-run, the file is deployed with mode 0600 automatically via the existing loop, with no bespoke per-file permission task added
